main_body: large half-timbered house with a multi-gabled red-brown tiled roof and chimney
top_band: red-brown and golden-yellow tiled roof slope from row 0 to row 42 on the main wings (and down to row 53 at the central gable peak / row 74 at the gable eaves)
evidence: The main wings show a deep foreshortened tiled roof from row 0 to 42, a dark eave line at row 42-43, an under-eave shadow band at rows 44-46, and a plaster/timber front wall from row 43 to 74 (and the central projecting gable continues down to row 106). Even the chimney at the top right shows its top opening.

style.evidence: The candidate is an authentic Beodeul house piece sharing the exact roof tile ramps (6 tones from pale yellow highlight to deep maroon shadow), speckled plaster texture, timber framing, and detailed doors/windows of the reference buildings.
